category: Branded search and legacy URL lifecycle
title: Two branded-search destinations point to independently confirmed NXDOMAIN hosts
confidence: High for returned search records and NXDOMAIN observed through audit resolver and Google Public DNS; intended retirement policy unresolved
template_or_page: Two unreachable search-discovered URLs on two subdomains. Two working admin redirects are separate context, not counted as broken endpoints.
evidence: evidence/query-log.json returns seller root and developer API records aged 4 months or last month. evidence/external-surface-probes.json records audit-resolver DNS failures. evidence/secondary-dns-check.json records Google Public DNS Status3 (NXDOMAIN) for both host A queries. Admin URLs instead redirect successfully to a noindex,nofollow accounts lookup page.
business_impact: A user following either observed search record cannot reach its destination at capture time. This is a confirmed broken discovery path; intended retirement remains unresolved. It does not show a private-console exposure, penalty or ranking loss.
recommended_fix: Confirm intended host lifecycle and ownership. Preserve working private-account returns. If the hosts are retired, choose truthful terminal handling or a genuinely relevant migration destination under normal release authorization and inspect owned indexing evidence. Do not reactivate frozen runtimes or blanket-redirect unrelated old paths to the homepage.
implementation_example: Maintain a reviewed URL disposition table: old URL, intended audience, current redirect/status, owner, target or terminal state, and verification evidence. No production configuration change is made by this audit.
owner_role: Platform/domain owner with SEO and identity owner
effort: 0.5–1 working day for disposition and owned indexing review if owner evidence is available; implementation and recrawl observation excluded. Second-resolver checks already completed.
dependencies: Current host ownership and intended retirement decision
Authorized Search Console access if available
Preservation of legitimate identity/private account journeys
validation_steps: After an authorized lifecycle change, recheck exact old URLs and intended terminal or redirect behavior using independent resolvers; preserve account returns/noindex behavior; inspect indexed state where available and repeat fixed branded queries after normal recrawl.
success_indicator: Both unreachable URL records have a verified lifecycle decision and intended handling. Unhelpful stale records diminish over observed recrawls without restoring deprecated runtimes or disrupting accounts.
failure_check: An automatic homepage redirect, recreated deprecated runtime or disrupted return path would be a failed remediation. Empty site: searches do not prove success.

category: Brand identity and external app presence
title: Live consumer Google Play listing uses the shared brand and legacy web/privacy destinations
confidence: High for direct listing content/links and both legacy destination HTTP captures; intended product relationship and ownership remain unverified
template_or_page: One public app listing with product/relationship ambiguity; two directly inspected legacy destinations. Parent owns a distinct privacy-route content finding to prevent duplicate counting.
evidence: evidence/play-listing-sanitized.json: live English listing200; consumer shopping/reels description; website/privacy anchors use letbuy-y.web.app. evidence/legacy-app-destinations.json: both exact URLs return200 title Create Next App, same ETag and matching captured merchant-landing text including old seller/processed-volume claims. Parent browser privacy verification is separate.
business_impact: The buyer-shopping app points to an older merchant landing, while its declared privacy URL serves matching captured landing HTML. That can confuse audience, availability and support expectations. Identity/ownership and truth of old outcome claims are not certified; buyer and merchant products may legitimately share a brand.
recommended_fix: Verify the listing/product owner, intended buyer-versus-merchant relationship, availability and lifecycle. Reconcile old merchant-result claims against real evidence. Coordinate any separately confirmed privacy-content repair with the privacy owner. Do not add sameAs or edit the app store listing solely from a name/package match.
implementation_example: Draft a product relationship table with audience, official app/package, owned website, privacy/controller notice, availability and support route; leave unverified cells explicitly unresolved.
owner_role: Product/brand owner with mobile release and privacy owner
effort: 0.5–1 working day for owner/account facts and draft copy, excluding legal approval, app-store publishing or engineering.
dependencies: Verified app and product ownership/identity facts
Privacy/controller review and correct public destinations
validation_steps: Owner verifies package/account relationship and intended audience. Check approved store labels and destinations; validate dedicated privacy content in raw and rendered states through the parent privacy finding; repeat quoted-brand searches after separately authorized publication.
success_indicator: Clear verified relationship and accurate reachable public destinations for the app; no unsupported sameAs or forced merging of distinct audiences.
failure_check: Changing the app listing before ownership is established or replacing consumer support with an unrelated merchant destination would be a failed correction.
